lines.text: Coca-Cola doesn't bottle most of the Coke you drink.
lines.say: Coca-Cola doesn't bottle most of the Coke you drink.

lines.text: In 2025, 85% of its drink volume came from concentrate sold to bottlers.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, eighty-five percent of its drink volume came from concentrate it sold to bottlers.

lines.text: Coca-Cola sells the syrup. Bottlers add water and sweetener, then bottle and sell it.
lines.say: Coca-Cola sells the syrup. Bottlers add water and sweetener, then bottle and sell it.

lines.text: That syrup business made 59% of Coca-Cola's $47.9B in 2025 revenue.
lines.say: That syrup business made fifty-nine percent of Coca-Cola's forty-seven point nine billion dollars in twenty twenty-five revenue.

lines.text: That share grew from 55% in 2019, partly as Coca-Cola sold bottling operations.
lines.say: That share grew from fifty-five percent in twenty nineteen, partly as Coca-Cola sold bottling operations.

lines.text: Coca-Cola's 2025 operating margin was 28.7%. The largest US Coke bottler ran about 13%.
lines.say: Why does it matter? Coca-Cola's twenty twenty-five operating margin was twenty-eight point seven percent. The largest US Coke bottler ran about thirteen percent.

lines.text: Bottlers carry the costly plants, trucks and workers. Coca-Cola keeps the brand and recipe.
lines.say: Bottlers carry the costly plants, trucks and workers. Coca-Cola keeps the brand and recipe.

lines.text: Its 10-K says concentrate earns higher margins than bottling. 2025 gross margin: 61.6%.
lines.say: Its filing says concentrate earns higher margins than bottling. Its twenty twenty-five gross margin was sixty-one point six percent.
